channel.title: Paper Pulse
channel.description: Keyword-based research paper aggregation from arXiv and IACR

item.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **MMDiff**, a multimodal model-diffing framework that trains multimodal sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to serve as feature-level interfaces for discovering and controlling MLLM behaviors. It enables three key capabilities: isolating features altered by multimodal training, detecting task-specific causal features via contrastive firing analysis, and controlling behaviors through feature removal or steering.
## Key Results Across LLaVA-MORE, PaliGemma 2, and InternVL3.5, MMDiff discovers sparse, causally specific features whose removal selectively degrades spatial understanding by 12%, OCR by 17%, and reduces multimodal safety attack success by 24%, without impacting VQA performance. Feature steering improves spatial and OCR accuracy by +3.6% and +1.8% over single-layer baselines.
## Significance This work demonstrates that multimodal SAEs extend beyond interpretability, offering practical mechanisms for auditing, steering, and controlling MLLMs toward safer and more capable generation.

item.title: From Values to Benchmarks: Evaluating Large Language Models for Governmental Use in Dutch
item.description:
**Core Contribution**: We introduce "Grip on LLMs," a value-driven evaluation framework for Dutch governmental use, co-developed with municipal domain experts. It operationalizes six dimensions—factuality, honesty, social bias, energy consumption, cost, and training-data transparency—into a benchmark suite covering 30+ multilingual and Dutch-specific models.
**Key Findings**: No model dominates across all dimensions; higher quality consistently trades off against environmental impact and cost, while bias remains orthogonal. Critically, factuality and honesty are governed by distinct model properties—being correct does not imply acknowledging ignorance. This distinction is vital for civil servants who must trust model uncertainty signals.
**Impact**: We release a public, non-technical model comparison dashboard to support diverse stakeholders in governmental LLM procurement, bridging the gap between technical benchmarks and public-administration values. This work provides a replicable template for non-English, value-sensitive AI evaluation.

item.title: GENCO - A Unified Neural Solver Embedded in a Development Framework for Steady-State Grid Analysis
item.description:
## Core Contribution We present **GENCO**, a unified neural solver for steady-state grid analysis (power flow, optimal power flow, state estimation) with a single architecture, plus the open-source **GridFM** development framework and large-scale benchmark datasets.
## Key Results - **PF**: Recovers full AC state (including voltage/reactive power) at DC-PF-level active power residuals; up to **30× faster** than Newton-Raphson, only 2× the runtime of DC-PF. - **OPF**: Up to **85× speedup** over IPOPT, with improved feasibility and optimality over DC-OPF. - **SE**: More robust than weighted least squares to noisy measurements and parameter errors, always producing high-quality estimates even when classical methods diverge.
## Impact This unified approach lowers entry barriers for power engineers and represents a significant step toward Grid Foundation Models, validated on both standard benchmarks and real Hydro-Québec SCADA data.

item.title: Fusion Training for Mathematical Generalization in Large Language Models
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper presents the first systematic study of **Thinking Mode Fusion (TMF)** training dynamics, focusing on how data ratios and training schedules affect mathematical reasoning performance.
## Key Findings 1. **Asymmetric interference**: Increasing non-thinking supervision reduces thinking-mode accuracy, but the reverse effect is minimal. 2. **Schedule-dependent trade-offs**: The optimal training schedule varies with data ratio—alternating training works best when thinking data dominates, while staged training mitigates performance loss when non-thinking data dominates. 3. **Quantified tension**: A significant negative correlation (~-0.6) exists between thinking and non-thinking supervision signals, confirming an inherent conflict between the two modes.
## Practical Impact Our results provide concrete guidance for designing effective TMF configurations in real-world LLM deployment. All resources are released via **Fusion Bench** (github.com/caocongfeng/Fusion-Bench) to facilitate further research and reproducibility.

item.title: SHE: Trajectory-driven Safety Harness Evolution for LLM Agents
item.description: **SHE** (Safety Harness Evolution) addresses the limitation of static LLM agent harnesses that cannot adapt to emerging risks. It decomposes the harness into four safety-attributed artifacts—System Prompt, Rule Bank, Safety Memory, and Tool Policy—enabling localized evolution with clear responsibility boundaries. An attribution-guided loop converts trajectory failures into structured diagnoses, learns artifact-specific boundary refinements, and selects evolved harnesses via safety-utility validation. On Agent-SafetyBench, SHE reduces attack success rate by **3.1×** compared to static SafeHarness while improving benign utility. The evolved harness generalizes to unseen risks on AgentHarm and transfers across agent models without further evolution, offering a scalable paradigm for dynamically safe LLM agents.

item.title: Energy-Structured Latent World Models with Neural Time Fields for Physically Constistent Open-World Motion Planning
item.description:
## Key Contribution We propose **Energy-Structured Latent World Model (ELWM)** with **Physics-Conditioned Neural Time Fields (PC-NTF)** for physically consistent open-world motion planning. ELWM explicitly encodes energy and momentum in latent states, ensuring strictly causal transitions via dissipation/control ports. PC-NTF integrates ELWM into arrival-time fields through the Eikonal equation, yielding physics-informed navigation policies.
**Results**: On held-out scenes, PC-NTF reduces motion-prediction NRMSE from 0.36 to 0.29, boosts navigation success from 81.3% to 89.7% (SPL: 0.64→0.73), and cuts physical collision rate from 12.1% to 5.8% with Eikonal residual dropping from 0.083 to 0.031. Our work demonstrates that embedding explicit physical structures into latent spaces intrinsically bridges predictive world models and safe, dynamically feasible motion planning.

item.title: ArchAgent v2: A Case Study with the Data Prefetching Championship
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper presents **ArchAgent v2**, a framework that scales automated microarchitecture search to multi-level data prefetching. Building on the single-level success of ArchAgent, we introduce **cascaded evolutionary search** (sequentially evolving and freezing per-level prefetchers) and a **hardware-realizability feedback loop** (embedding real-time area estimation into evolution).
## Key Results Under identical DPC4 competition rules, ArchAgent v2 automatically designs a three-level prefetcher that **outperforms the winning human-designed solution**: achieving 3.8% geometric-mean IPC speedup over baseline (0.3% over prior champion BertiGO), and notably **4.6% speedup on low-bandwidth single-core** configurations versus BertiGO's 2.6%. Multi-core evolution remains challenging due to simulation latency.
## Significance Analysis of 12,000+ candidate designs reveals how automated evolutionary agents synthesize complex microarchitectural logic, positioning agentic discovery as a practical tool for computer architects beyond human intuition.

item.title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper exposes a critical architectural vulnerability in proprietary LLM APIs: encrypted reasoning traces (chain-of-thought) returned to clients are interchangeable across sessions, users, and models within the same provider. We exploit this to build a scalable decryption jailbreak by injecting a strong model's encrypted trace into a weaker model from the same provider, forcing it to output the reasoning verbatim in plaintext—without ever directly attacking the stronger model.
## Key Results We demonstrate four attack vectors: (1) bypassing anti-distillation to extract proprietary reasoning from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google; (2) large-scale private data extraction—decoding 315,320 public reasoning blocks yielded 367 PII artifacts and 182 credentials; (3) exposing hazardous hidden reasoning even when final outputs are safe; and (4) invisible prompt injection via encrypted blocks. We propose concrete cryptographic and system-level mitigations following responsible disclosure.

item.title: Towards Expert-level Medical AI for Real-time Video Consultations
item.description: This study presents the first demonstration of expert-level AI in real-time clinical video consultations using AMIE (Video), a Gemini-based multi-agent system integrating low-latency dialogue, clinical reasoning, and real-time audio-visual perception. In a randomized OSCE study with 30 primary care physicians, 15 patient actors, and 100 clinical scenarios, clinical evaluators rated AMIE (Video) on par or better than physicians in history-taking, diagnosis, management, and physical observation, while patient actors preferred its approach to assessing and explaining conditions. However, physicians were preferred for rapport building, and limitations remain in fine anatomical precision and subtle affective nuances. These findings mark a significant milestone toward AI systems capable of augmenting care across the sensory complexity of clinical practice, though further research is needed before real-world translation.

item.title: Agentic Harnesses: LLM-Driven Verification Layers for Robot Autonomy
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces a **novel LLM-driven verification layer** positioned between robot planning and execution, addressing the critical gap in action feasibility validation. Unlike prior work focused solely on task execution, this middleware evaluates action permissibility before plans reach low-level controls.
## Method The system employs an **LLM-as-a-Judge ensemble** that combines chain-of-thought reasoning across multiple models, integrating mixture-of-experts and self-consistency strategies. It gates plans through three outcomes: **approve**, **reject for reformulation**, or **escalate to human review**.
## Key Results Experiments demonstrate **~85% precision** across all decision categories, **97% containment of adversarial attacks**, with minimal errors between accept/reject decisions—errors mainly concentrate at the escalation boundary.
## Significance This work pioneers a scalable safety mechanism for robot autonomy, enhancing both adversarial robustness and ethical compliance while maintaining operational efficiency. The framework offers a practical pathway toward trustworthy autonomous systems in real-world deployments.

item.title: Multi-Agent AI Safety as an Institutional Design Problem
item.description: This paper introduces POLIS, a research program on algorithmic institutions for multi-agent systems, investigating which institutional components ensure safety and how. Using a frozen 5,280-episode suite across four model families, we test delegation workflows with varied rule formulations, authority states, and post-block pathways. Key results: a detailed constitutional prompt and a provenance-aware executable guard both achieve 0/384 violations, though the guard blocks 51 prohibited attempts (44 later complete safely). Local-state guards fail specifically when routine transformations alter visible policy while origin authority remains fixed—admitting violations in 22/96 laundering scenarios versus 0/96 with provenance enforcement (p=4.77×10⁻⁷). A resource-allocation test shows revealing numerical caps changes agent requests. We conclude that identical violation rates can mask fundamentally different mechanisms: institutional safety depends not only on rules but on trusted authority states and available recovery paths after blocking.

item.title: Distill Skills into Weights, Not Prompts: Abstract Skills as Privileged Signals for On-Policy Self-Distillation
item.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards loses group-relative signals when rollout groups are uniformly correct or wrong—accounting for 63.0–68.0% of groups in our experiments. We propose **SKALD** (Skill-Anchored Latent Distillation), an on-policy self-distillation framework using two context views of the same Qwen3-Base model: a question-only student and a teacher conditioned on an abstract, answer-filtered skill card. The student trains on its own prefixes, transferring skill-induced advantages into shared weights without privileged test-time inputs. An annealed exponentially tilted objective stabilizes context mismatch, converging to teacher cross-entropy and recovering forward-KL student gradients; an empirical gate activates distillation only when verified rollouts estimate positive teacher advantage. Across five held-out math benchmarks, SKALD improves avg@8 over GRPO by +2.46, +4.85, and +12.01 at 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B scales. At 1.7B, zero-variance-only distillation recovers 84.7% of the full gain, while SKALD remains +4.06 above FLOP-matched GRPO and +3.77 above contextual skill exposure. Abstract skills thus provide dense supervision exactly where group-relative rewards become uninformative.

item.title: MedPixel: A Unified Pixel-Language Model for Medical Reasoning and Segmentation
item.description:
## Core Contribution We present **MedPixel**, a unified medical pixel-language model that bridges clinical language understanding and pixel-level segmentation through a shared language-mask interface. To overcome the supervision mismatch between segmentation and vision-language datasets, we introduce **MedPLG-440K**, approximately 440K pixel-language task samples generated via a clinically motivated synthesis pipeline without external LLM annotation.
## Key Innovation MedPixel employs joint multi-task supervised fine-tuning followed by **Pixel-Level Preference Optimization**, which leverages ground-truth masks as offline verifiers to derive response preferences from mask quality. This enables the model to handle a broad task spectrum, including explicit grounding, implicit reasoning, spatial interaction, grounded explanation, and medical VQA.
## Results MedPixel achieves strong performance across both pixel-level prediction and response generation, demonstrating effective zero-shot transfer to external grounding benchmarks and robustness to imperfect spatial prompts. Code and checkpoints will be released.

item.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces **parameter-space exploration** for LLM reinforcement learning, complementing traditional action-space methods (e.g., temperature scaling) that cannot reorder tokens and thus limit exploration diversity. The authors propose **3PO (Perturbed Parameter Policy Optimization)**, a family of methods that sample diverse policy parameters from a posterior to generate rollouts, with different sampling strategies and rollout grouping for reward estimation.
## Key Results Experiments on OLMo-3-1025-7B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B across mathematical reasoning and code generation show that 3PO **consistently outperforms standard GRPO** in average downstream performance at nearly identical FLOPs cost. Moreover, multi-parameter sampling **substantially reduces** zero-advantage groups and malformed rollouts during training compared to GRPO and action-space baselines.
## Significance This work provides strong evidence that parameter-space exploration is a viable and effective lever for improving RLVR, offering a more robust exploration mechanism that could mitigate training instability in LLM reinforcement learning.

item.title: KGCaRe: Explainable Complex Conditional Question Answering using Automatic Knowledge Graph Construction and Context Retrieval with LLMs
item.description:
## Core Contribution We propose **KGCaRe**, a hybrid framework that enhances complex conditional question answering by combining neural retrieval with symbolic reasoning over LLM-generated knowledge graphs. The system automatically constructs domain-specific KGs from documents via multi-prompt extraction, stores them in a graph database, and employs LLM-guided iterative graph traversal with a novel "clue entity" mechanism to extract relevant triples while pruning noise. Retrieved graph paths and semantic text passages are jointly fed into custom prompts to generate explainable answers.
## Key Findings Evaluated on two complex conditional QA datasets, KGCaRe consistently outperforms existing baselines (including Vanilla LLM, RAG, and Think-on-Graph) across four LLMs (Mistral, Mixtral, GPT-3.5, GPT-4o). The results demonstrate that augmenting RAG with both unstructured and structured knowledge significantly improves reasoning accuracy. The complete software pipeline is publicly released to facilitate reproducibility and further research.

item.title: MoNo: Multiscale Optimal Transport Neural Operator for Solving PDEs on General Geometries
item.description: ## Core Contribution We propose **MoNo**, a progressive multiscale neural operator that solves PDEs on general geometries via stable latent-space construction. Its key innovation, **CoTAP**, formulates cross-scale token assignment as entropy-regularized optimal transport, ensuring balanced bidirectional projections and preventing token collapse in deep latent spaces. This enables efficient hierarchical learning of long-range interactions. Experiments show MoNo outperforms state-of-the-art neural operators in both accuracy and computational efficiency. Code: https://github.com/ZijiangY1116/MoNo

item.title: Defining Decentralization: An Ontological Perspective
item.description:
## Defining Decentralization: An Ontological Perspective
**Motivation:** Despite half a century of use in computer science, decentralization lacks a universally accepted definition across communication systems, creating inconsistencies in analysis and weakening formal reasoning—especially critical with the rise of decentralized AI paradigms.
**Approach:** We formalize this gap as the *Decentralization Problem* and propose a **graph-based ontology** that defines decentralization as a *relational, subject-specific property* of systems, formally distinguishing it from distribution. Two novel metrics—**Void Tolerance** and **Imperviousness**—enable quantitative evaluation, supported by a browser-based tool for automated classification.
**Results:** Instantiations on federated learning and blockchain demonstrate consistent, comparable assessments where prior definitions fail or conflict. This work provides a **domain-independent foundation** for analyzing decentralization across heterogeneous systems, addressing a critical theoretical gap in computer communication research.

item.title: SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper proposes **SR-OPSD (Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation)** to address the instability of standard on-policy self-distillation, where the self-teacher policy co-evolves with the student, making fixed projection objectives unreliable.
## Method SR-OPSD introduces a token-level variational characterization that formulates the effective distillation target as a **geometric interpolation** between the self-teacher and a reference policy. It further generalizes the projection geometry using the **Rényi divergence family**, decoupling *where* the adaptive target lies (controlled by the interpolation coefficient) from *how* the student is projected (controlled by the Rényi order).
## Results Extensive experiments across scientific evaluation, mathematical reasoning, and code generation with multiple LLMs demonstrate that SR-OPSD achieves **state-of-the-art or competitive performance** in various settings, confirming its robustness and effectiveness.

item.title: Rethinking Factor Sharing in Federated LoRA: A Rank-Aware Adaptive Approach
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper rethinks factor-sharing strategies in federated LoRA by theoretically proving that **Share-A/Local-B** and **Share-B/Local-A** require a common rank-$r$ input-side vs. output-side subspace, respectively, leading to different projection residuals. The optimal strategy is the one minimizing the aggregate residual across clients.
## Proposed Method We introduce **FedAS-LoRA**, which adaptively selects the sharing side *before training* using a novel **Rank-Aware Shared-Subspace Sufficiency (RSS)** metric. RSS leverages frozen LLM representations to assess whether a shared rank-$r$ input subspace suffices for local data distributions, enabling data-driven factor selection without training overhead.
## Key Results Experiments across diverse tasks, data distributions, LoRA ranks, and participation settings confirm that RSS accurately predicts the preferred strategy, and FedAS-LoRA consistently outperforms fixed-sharing baselines, demonstrating the practical value of adaptive factor sharing in federated fine-tuning.

item.title: Model Discovery Agent: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic world models
item.description:
**Core Contribution**: We introduce the **Model Discovery Agent (MDA)**, a framework that couples LLM-based structure proposal with Bayesian machinery (SMC, SBI, and VoI) to discover mechanistic world models from minimal interventions, operating in the M-open setting where the truth may lie outside the current hypothesis class.
**Key Mechanism**: MDA alternates between predictive checks (flagging model inadequacy), LLM-driven hypothesis expansion, and VoI-optimized experiments. This creates a **discovery-design feedback loop**: designed experiments validate proposed mechanisms, and validated mechanisms improve predictions, enabling further discoveries from residuals.
**Results**: On three benchmarks (physics DPbench, chemistry CHEMbench, and a new biology benchmark HHbench for partially observed neuron electrophysiology), MDA achieves **state-of-the-art data efficiency** and reliable interventional forecasting, demonstrating that LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design can substantially reduce experimental cost while maintaining mechanistic fidelity.

item.title: Open Evaluation Agent: Efficient and Promptable Evaluation of Visual Generative Models
item.description:
## Core Contribution We propose **Evaluation Agent**, a human-like framework for efficient, dynamic, and multi-round evaluation of visual generative models. It decomposes natural-language requests into sub-aspects, generates targeted prompts, samples outputs, invokes suitable tools, and iteratively refines its plan based on observed evidence—covering both benchmark dimensions and open-ended user concerns.
## Key Results The agent reduces evaluation time to **10% of traditional methods** while delivering comparable results. To mitigate dependence on proprietary backbones, we introduce **Open-EA** (trained as EA-3B from Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct) using a new corpus, EA-CoT-10K, derived from multi-round rollouts. Experiments validate the API-based agent on established T2I/T2V benchmarks and show partial cross-family policy transfer for Open-EA across four in-domain and three out-of-domain T2V generator families.

item.title: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper tackles **GUI grounding hallucination** in multimodal LLMs by proposing a **regression-free, layout-aware matching framework**. The key idea is to decouple semantic parsing from coordinate localization: a frozen MLLM first expands abstract user instructions into structured visual descriptions rich in layout cues; then a dedicated grounding model performs localization by **matching against layout-prior candidates** (e.g., clickable region boxes), without learning any coordinate regression parameters. This design inherently suppresses hallucinations and avoids expensive fine-tuning, requiring only binary text/icon labels for training.
## Key Results On ScreenSpot-Pro, the method improves grounding accuracy by **over 20%** compared to end-to-end systems; on Mind2Web, it raises success rate and element selection rate by **more than 15%**. These results demonstrate that decoupling instruction understanding from layout-aware matching effectively resolves the core challenges of GUI interaction, offering a scalable and reliable paradigm for vision-based GUI agents.

item.title: NeuroRefiner: Morphology-Aware Multi-Agent Refinement for 3D Fluorescence Microscopy Neuron Segmentation
item.description:
## Overview This paper presents **NeuroRefiner**, a multi-agent system for accurate 3D neuron segmentation in fluorescence microscopy, addressing the challenge of preserving both local details and global topology in sparse, elongated neuronal structures.
## Method NeuroRefiner formalizes the expert workflow of iterative global observation and local editing through three collaborative agents that diagnose topological errors, generate correction instructions, and validate refinement quality. A dedicated 3D U-Net tool, **TopoRefineNet**, leverages cross-modality feature fusion to execute instruction-guided mask refinement via multi-round agent reasoning and voxel-level editing.
## Results Experiments on BigNeuron, CWMBS, and ZBFWB datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, with a notable **3.02% F1-score improvement** on the challenging ZBFWB dataset, confirming enhanced topological accuracy and interpretability.

item.title: Measuring the Wrong Thing: Internal Harmfulness Scores Anti-Rank Successful Jailbreaks
item.description:
## Core Finding Internal safety scores evaluate prompts *before* generation, yet their validation metric—separating harmful from benign *intent*—does not transfer to predicting *successful jailbreaks*. Harmful intent is a property of the prompt; jailbreak success is an outcome produced later by the target model, decoding policy, and judge.
## Method & Result We introduce **Active Attention Probing**, a fixed content-independent measurement coordinate, and pair every base goal with plain vs. wrapped versions on real model completions. On Llama, wrapping *raises* harmful generation from 0.05 to 0.27 while *lowering* harmful-intent AUROC from 0.936 to 0.803—attacks become more dangerous as prompts look safer. Among wrapped harmful prompts, outcome AUROC is **0.220**, ranking successful attacks *below* failed ones. This reversal persists across 3 models, 7 attack families, and 2 judges, reproduced via rare-token, passive, and detector-derived channels.
## Implication Distribution shift degrades calibration before ranking. A filter tuned on the wrong quantity spends its false-positive budget on attacks that would fail anyway—**jailbreaks anti-rank against internal harmfulness scores**, questioning the foundational assumption of prompt-only safety filtering.

item.title: TSPORec: Token Selection via Preference Optimization for LLM-Based Sequential Recommendation
item.description:
## Core Contribution We propose **TSPORec**, a novel token selection approach via preference optimization for LLM-based sequential recommendation. Instead of truncating item descriptions to the first few tokens, TSPORec precisely identifies the most informative tokens across the entire text, achieving both higher accuracy and lower inference cost.
## Method & Results A three-stage pipeline with a novel proxy reward enables efficient token selection without full model inference. Extensive experiments across two models and datasets show that TSPORec improves recommendation performance by up to **31.25%** and computational efficiency by up to **63.4%** compared to six baseline methods. This demonstrates that selective token reading outperforms both full-text and prefix-truncation strategies. Code is publicly available.
## Impact TSPORec offers a practical, cost-effective paradigm for LLM-based recommender systems, particularly valuable for long-text item descriptions, and opens a new direction integrating token-level selection with preference optimization.

item.title: From Sweep to Seam: Interleaved Cross-Block Post-Training Quantization
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces **Interleaved Cross-Block Quantization (ICBQ)**, a scheduling modification for block-wise post-training quantization of large language models. Unlike the sequential baseline that sweeps a two-block window once, ICBQ revisits each seam (boundary pair) between consecutive chunks twice—once at the end of the current chunk and again at the start of the next—while preserving the local two-block objective and reusing existing calibration inputs.
## Key Results Under stated contraction and smoothness assumptions, the authors derive a depth-wise error bound showing that seam revisits amplify the propagated term but keep the residual bounded independent of depth. Experiments demonstrate that ICBQ reduces ternary-quantization perplexity versus the sequential cross-block baseline, achieves finite perplexity in configurations where the baseline severely degrades, and extends effectively to 3-bit and 2-bit GPTQ. The method offers a zero-overhead accuracy boost purely via traversal-order modification, providing both theoretical insight and practical gains for extreme low-bit compression.

item.title: Illusion or Integrity? Geometrical Consistency Metric for AIGC Video Quality Evaluation
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **GeoCon-Bench**, a novel benchmark that evaluates AIGC video quality by quantifying **geometric consistency** across frames—a proxy for physical-law compliance. Unlike existing VQA metrics focusing on visual appeal or semantic alignment, our method estimates global motion via translation, fits homography/fundamental matrix models from background correspondences, and reports inlier ratio plus geometric error.
## Key Results Experiments on state-of-the-art AIGC models demonstrate that GeoCon-Bench reliably distinguishes generated videos by their adherence to real-world physical rules. We release a dataset of 20 scenes across six motion categories, providing a complementary quantitative tool for video generation evaluation and model optimization. This work bridges the gap between perceptual quality and physical integrity in AIGC assessment.

item.title: Bidirectional Context Self-Distillation for Reinforcement Learning of Skill-Based LLM Agents
item.description:
## Core Contribution We propose **BCSD (Bidirectional Context Self-Distillation)**, a framework combining self-distillation with reinforcement learning to train LLM agents to better utilize external natural-language skills. Unlike prior self-distillation methods relying on a single privileged context, BCSD evaluates each trajectory from two complementary views: an augmented view with high-level Meta-Skill guidance and a reduced view pruning general guidance to highlight task-specific skills. Their token-level signals are combined to rescale the RL advantage.
## Key Results Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop show BCSD achieves the strongest overall performance across model scales, enabling more effective skill utilization. Ablation studies confirm the complementary contributions of both context views. Code will be released for full reproducibility.

item.title: ELBench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Education-Facing Large Language Models
item.description:
## Overview We introduce **ELBench**, the first benchmark that evaluates education-facing large language models (LLMs) under a unified protocol across four key dimensions: general capability, safety & trustworthiness, basic education, and high-level cultivation. Unlike prior benchmarks that assess these aspects in isolation, ELBench integrates curated public sources with newly synthesized safety and cultivation data to provide a holistic profile of educational suitability.
## Key Findings Evaluating nine models (seven frontier general-purpose, two education-specialized), we report three main results: **(1)** Module-level profiles are more informative than aggregate scores—top models are statistically tied overall yet differ substantially by module, and safety is strongly anti-correlated with teaching practicality (r = -0.83). **(2)** Chinese-developed models lead the safety module (the most discriminative), especially on region-specific normative content. **(3)** Education-specialized models lead neither education module, and all models share a systematic blind spot in high-level cultivation tasks—uniformly favoring pedagogical style over goal-fit, yielding low non-discriminative scores. This raises an open question: do domain-tuned models truly keep pace with frontier systems in education? ELBench offers a more granular tool for reliable educational AI deployment.

item.title: TCS-BENCH: Benchmarking State-of-the-Art Generative AI Theoretical Computer Science Research Ability
item.description: We introduce **TCS-Bench**, the first benchmark specifically designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on research-level theoretical computer science (TCS) proof generation. The benchmark comprises theorem-proving tasks extracted from top-tier venues (STOC, FOCS, SODA), each providing sufficient context for self-contained proof derivation. We assess state-of-the-art models using a two-stage pipeline: an automated verification agent checks proof correctness, and this verifier is calibrated against human-expert judgments on a labeled subset. Our reference verifier achieves over **90% accuracy** on expert-labeled pairs, demonstrating reliable automated evaluation. Results reveal that current LLMs struggle with multi-step logical chains and creative construction in complex proofs, highlighting critical gaps in deep reasoning capabilities. TCS-Bench offers a standardized tool for advancing AI-assisted mathematical research.

item.title: verdi: retrieval is not transfer for continual world model optimization
item.description:
## Core Insight VERDI challenges the assumption that successful optimization strategies are directly reusable, proposing **"retrieval is not transfer"**—retrieved experience serves only as a hypothesis until validated on the target model.
## Method It builds an **Optimization Fingerprint** via shared inference-time probes to characterize world models, retrieves ranked prior strategies, and admits them only after passing a frozen target-side verifier. Contradictions between nearby fingerprints trigger probe evolution, refining the diagnostic representation continuously.
## Results On Ctrl-World, Cosmos, and RoboCoin benchmarks, VERDI cuts search cost by 68% and GPU cost by 69%, reduces negative transfer from 0.34 to 0.06, and achieves 83% sign accuracy in predicting transfer outcomes. This establishes the first evidence-licensed framework for continual world model optimization, transforming optimization knowledge into cumulative scientific assets.

item.title: Carnot: Interpretable, Interactive, and Optimized Execution of Deep Research Queries
item.description: ## Summary Enterprises increasingly query data lakes via AI agents, but these systems often operate as opaque black boxes, hiding intermediate reasoning and lacking cost/latency controls. We present **Carnot**, an interactive execution engine that compiles natural language requests into physical execution graphs displayed in a notebook interface. Users can critique plans, incrementally execute operators, inspect intermediate data, or directly edit code and semantic instructions. A built-in optimizer adjusts execution under user-specified cost or latency constraints. Demonstrated on real enterprise workloads, Carnot transforms opaque AI analytics into transparent, verifiable, and efficient workflows, giving analysts agency to intercept errors and correct trajectories in real time.

item.title: Renormalising Generative Models for Active Inference: Foundations, Derivations, and Verification
item.description: ## Core Contribution This paper provides a **self-contained, derivation-oriented account** of Renormalising Generative Models (RGMs) for active inference, together with an open, verified implementation. It clarifies how hierarchical structures are built, how beliefs and actions are updated, and how information flows across levels—explicitly addressing discrepancies between published equations and reference code. By decoupling the theory from its original specialised software context, the work makes RGMs more **transparent, auditable, and reproducible**, significantly lowering practical barriers to entry. This foundation enables future quantitative benchmarking and broader adoption of RGMs in machine-learning research.

item.title: Build it, Break it, Repeat: Benchmarking and improving LLM-manipulated disinformation detection in social media posts
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces **BiBiR (Build, Break, Repeat)**, an iterative adversarial framework for stress-testing LLM-manipulated disinformation detectors on social media. Unlike static benchmarks, BiBiR repeatedly transforms posts to evade detection and retrains detectors across five iterations.
## Key Results - **Best attack** combined back-translation with LLM persona-based rewriting, achieving a **95% label flip rate** while preserving original post semantics. - **Best defense** used a triplet contrastive model with dynamic anchor switching (DASS), reaching **72.68% average accuracy**—15 points higher than a strong fine-tuned baseline under the most challenging attacks. - Iterative evaluation exposes detector weaknesses and drives robustness gains, but **semantic preservation analysis** is essential to distinguish valid evasion from meaning-altering transformations.
## Significance BiBiR offers a dynamic evaluation paradigm for disinformation detection, highlighting the trade-off between adversarial robustness and semantic fidelity—critical for deploying trustworthy social media moderation systems.

item.title: Learning Preference Adaptation for Large Language Model Personalization via Verbal Reinforcement Learning
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **AlignXada**, a training-free meta-learning framework for *task-specific preference adaptation* in LLM personalization. It learns reusable textual refinement policies via verbal reinforcement learning, automatically converting universal user preference summaries into compact, task-conditioned profiles that preserve decision-relevant evidence while removing redundant context.
## Key Results Across 13 tasks and 3 downstream models (39 task–model cells), AlignXada achieves an average gain of **3.82 points**, improving 33 cells while retaining only **22.8%** of original profile tokens, and outperforms RAG in 36 cells. Faithfulness analysis confirms refined profiles remain grounded in source preferences, suggesting profile-side adaptation complements universal memory construction for lifelong personalized agents. The method is parameter-free and directly applicable to any LLM.

item.title: MixFormer: Linear Transformer with Mixture of Memory Experts
item.description:
## Core Contribution We propose **MixFormer**, a linear Transformer integrating a **Mixture-of-Memory-Experts (MoE)** mechanism to overcome the limited adaptivity and constrained capacity of existing State Space Models. The model maintains differentiated memory states via collaborating experts and introduces **Time-Aware Linear Attention (TALA)** with learnable exponential decay and positional biases for dynamic memory updates.
## Key Results Experiments on long-sequence text and image generation demonstrate that MixFormer achieves **significant performance gains** over baselines while effectively mitigating memory dilution in ultra-long context modeling. This work provides a more **sustainable computational backbone** for next-generation web infrastructure, validating the effectiveness of expert-based memory management in linear attention architectures.

item.title: RecoverFly: A Failure-Aware Reinforcement Learning Post-Training Framework for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
item.description:
## Abstract
**RecoverFly** is a failure-aware reinforcement learning (RL) post-training framework for end-to-end UAV vision-language-action (UAV-VLA) policies. It addresses key limitations of behavior-cloning objectives in closed-loop navigation by introducing three innovations: token-level RL for stable optimization of grammar-constrained autoregressive actions, a failure-revisit mechanism that strengthens corrective learning and sample efficiency, and a two-stage long-tail scene curriculum with reference-policy regularization to improve adaptation while preventing capability loss. On the TravelUAV benchmark, RecoverFly achieves state-of-the-art performance across seen, unseen-map, and unseen-object splits. Using only ~30% of the training-set size as rollout budget, it improves success rate by **3.12–8.37 percentage points** over the AerialVLA baseline, demonstrating robust generalization and practical efficiency for real-world UAV navigation.

item.title: Learning to Modulate, Not to Cycle: Soft Actor---Critic Recovers Inverter-Style Heat-Pump Control
item.description:
## Key Contribution This paper addresses compressor wear caused by on-off cycling in residential heat pumps. We augment the control reward with a levelised cycling penalty and compare Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) versus Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) on the identical BOPTEST hydronic benchmark.
## Main Results - **SAC** learns a continuous modulation policy that keeps the compressor permanently engaged (inverter-style), achieving **zero start-ups per day**. - **PPO** collapses to bang-bang control, cycling even more than the baseline without penalty. - On the BOPTEST emulator, SAC reduces thermal discomfort by **90.7%** with only an 11.5% cost increase, while eliminating all baseline cycling.
## Implication We show that the choice of RL algorithm—not just reward shaping—is decisive for obtaining smooth, wear-free compressor control. SAC’s stochastic policy and entropy regularisation promote gentle modulation, whereas PPO’s deterministic updates lead to aggressive switching. This provides a practical guideline for deploying RL on compressor-based HVAC systems.

item.title: WDL-OPD: Weak-Driven On-Policy Distillation via Mixture-Constrained Co-Training
item.description:
## Core Contribution WDL-OPD introduces a mixture-constrained co-training framework with two trainable policies—an anchor policy for trajectory generation and an auxiliary policy for state evaluation—jointly aligned to a frozen teacher via reverse KL divergence. This design creates branch-level degrees of freedom absent in static deltas, stabilizing the on-policy distillation loop.
## Key Results At 1.7B and 4B scales, WDL-OPD consistently yields the strongest student checkpoints across four scale-domain settings. MATH500 accuracy improves from 0.630 to 0.685 (4B) and from 0.521 to 0.585 (1.7B). In code generation, all seven single-policy baselines suffer entropy growth or trajectory collapse, while co-training achieves development scores of 0.637 and 0.375.
## Scope Given uncontrolled curriculum/initialization differences in some baselines, these results support a stabilization hypothesis rather than a universal causal claim. The paper provides the exact algorithm, failure evidence, and a controlled comparison matrix for independent verification.

item.title: Coupled Graph--Policy Distillation for Personalized Medication Safety in Older Adults with Multimorbidity
item.description: ## Summary **Background**: LLM agents can support medication review between visits, but safe prescribing for older adults with multimorbidity depends on omitted conditions, drugs, and geriatric risks. **Method**: We present **ATLAS**, a coupled graph-policy distillation framework. It structures guideline evidence as a medication-safety graph, uses targeted questions to update patient state, and distills relevant relations into a patient-specific medication conflict graph (PMCG). A risk-first multi-agent policy then screens contraindications, assesses cautions/monitoring, identifies safer alternatives, and verifies the final plan. We also introduce **GeriMedBench**, an interactive benchmark for safety-critical information acquisition. **Results**: Across three benchmarks (European non-interactive, Asian interactive, Asian cross-guideline), ATLAS achieved the strongest complete-decision performance. On the European non-interactive benchmark, it outperformed the best proprietary LLM baseline by **53.73 points in Strict Success Rate** and **14.63 points in overall safety reasoning score**, with zero unsafe recommendations. Blinded clinicians rated ATLAS higher on all five criteria, flagging unsafe suggestions in only 1 ATLAS case vs. 2 Gemini cases. **Conclusion**: ATLAS demonstrates that coupling guideline graphs with dynamic patient-state distillation enables safer, more explainable medication decisions for complex older adults.

item.title: Listen, See and Track: Spatio-Temporal Audio-Visual Sound Event Reasoning for Omni-Modal Language Models
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper tackles the **spatio-temporal audio-visual sound event reasoning** problem—jointly identifying *what* sounds, *where* it is, and *how* it moves—a capability absent in existing audio-language and vision-language models.
## Key Deliverables - **ST-OmniQA**: A new benchmark with 40K panoramic videos and 400K QA pairs, organized into four progressive capability levels (recognition, direction-of-arrival, distance, trajectory, and temporally-grounded reasoning), using synchronized first-order Ambisonics audio. - **ST-Omni-R1**: A model integrating FOA-derived semantic/trajectory representations with panoramic visual context, trained via progressive curriculum learning and reasoning-tree reinforcement learning.
## Results & Impact ST-Omni-R1 achieves **77.83% average semantic accuracy** across all levels, significantly outperforming the best baseline (37.28%). Transfer experiments on three public spatial-audio benchmarks confirm the learned representations generalize well. This work establishes a standardized evaluation and strong baseline for dynamic sound source understanding in omni-modal language models.

item.title: ZetaGPT: A Reference Implementation of Positional--Encoding--Free State--Space--Attention Language Models
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **ZetaGPT**, the first open-source small language model that eliminates explicit positional encodings entirely. Instead of learned embeddings or rotary encodings, each model block applies a **causal state-space equation** before self-attention, allowing recurrent dynamics to implicitly encode token order into representations. This design preserves the expressive power of attention while removing architectural dependence on positional information.
## Key Results The model provides a fully open-sourced, end-to-end training pipeline—covering dataset construction, tokenizer training, pretraining, SFT, RLHF, and pure-RL-driven chain-of-thought reasoning. As a compact reference implementation, ZetaGPT enables reproducible research and rapid prototyping for positional-encoding-free architectures, demonstrating that sequential information can be intrinsically modeled through state dynamics rather than externally injected biases.

item.title: LITEWAY: LIghtweight HAR via Temporal Efficient highWAY
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **LITEWAY**, a modality-agnostic fully convolutional framework for wearable HAR that replaces recurrent temporal modeling (GRU/LSTM) with structured convolutional decomposition, enabling high parallelism and low inference latency.
## Key Results Evaluated on 16 HAR datasets against TinyHAR, TinierHAR, and MLP-HAR, LITEWAY achieves: - **Competitive macro F1** while reducing model size by **4.06×-9.52×** (Light) and **3.87×-9.07×** (Full) versus TinyHAR/TinierHAR. - **Energy reduction** of **2.29×-3.14×** (Light) and **1.46×-2.01×** (Full) in deployment tests.
## Significance This work demonstrates that efficient fully convolutional temporal modeling is a viable alternative to recurrent designs for edge-based HAR, offering a strong trade-off among accuracy, model compactness, and energy efficiency. Code is publicly available.

item.title: Sign Language Recognition Using Original and Synthetic Depth Image Based Point Cloud Data Models
item.description: This study investigates sign language recognition using point cloud data derived from both original and synthetic depth images. Depth images were generated from RGB inputs using the Depth Anything V2 network, and three datasets (Real-time ASL Fingerspelling, KArSL, AUTSL) were evaluated with multiple PointNet architectures. Three data models—frame-based, Point Gesture Map, and LSTM—were compared for classification performance. Results show that both original and synthetic depth-based point clouds achieve acceptable accuracy in most models, with original depth data generally outperforming synthetic counterparts. However, in certain models, synthetic depth data yielded superior results, highlighting its potential as a viable alternative when real depth data is unavailable. This work demonstrates the feasibility of using synthetic depth point clouds for sign language recognition, offering a practical solution for expanding limited depth-annotated datasets.

item.title: Monotonicity-Guided Bottom-Up Petri Net Discovery: The SPECpp Framework
item.description:
## Summary
Process discovery remains a central challenge in process mining. This paper introduces **SPECpp**, a monotonicity-guided bottom-up framework for Petri net discovery. Unlike top-down approaches (e.g., Inductive Miner) that rely on predefined constructs, SPECpp leverages monotonic properties of individual places to let complex structures—including free-choice and long-term dependencies—emerge organically. The key difficulty lies in the exponential search space of candidate places. SPECpp implements resource-aware strategies to efficiently explore this space, supporting rapid experimentation. Evaluated on both synthetic and real-life event logs, SPECpp demonstrates superior model precision and generalization compared to top-down baselines, particularly for logs with concurrency and long-distance dependencies. The framework offers a flexible, scalable alternative for discovering high-quality process models under time and resource constraints.

item.title: Imaginative Generative AI: Crossing the Entropy Wall into Worlds Beyond Imitation
item.description: This paper introduces **Imaginative Generative AI (IGA)**, a framework that reframes diversity as a design target rather than an implicit byproduct of imitation. IGA selects, among distributions close to a reference, one whose spectral diversity (measured by von Neumann entropy of the kernel covariance operator) reaches a prescribed level. The **Entropy Wall**—defined by the data distribution's spectral entropy—separates two regimes: below it, IGA performs diversity repair to recover variation lost by learned generators; beyond it, IGA deliberately departs from the data to achieve imaginative generation with greater representation-relative diversity. Theoretically, under a KL anchor to a pretrained generator, the optimum satisfies a self-consistent exponential-tilt relation, yielding **IGA Guidance**, a retraining-free inference-time method for score-based and diffusion models (including DDPM/DDIM). Experiments on synthetic and vision benchmarks demonstrate effective diversity repair within the wall and controlled spectral extrapolation beyond it, establishing a unified path from imitation to imagination.

item.title: OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces **OpenLoopEvolve (OLE)**, a verifiable self-evolution framework centered on the **Loop Policy** for long-horizon complex tasks. OLE encapsulates agent behaviors (observation, planning, memory, action, verification, recovery, stopping, and budget control) as versioned, lineage-tracked policy assets, supporting both **online** (feedback-driven candidate generation) and **offline** (trace-mining from archived evidence) evolution modes.
## Key Mechanism & Results Both modes share a unified evolution pipeline: LLM-proposed candidates → Champion-Challenger paired evaluation → robust release, with online rollback to parent versions upon degradation. On the YC-Bench benchmark, both modes improved aggregate task performance, success rate, and risk metrics over a fixed baseline policy. The results demonstrate that treating loop policies as governable assets enables systematic accumulation, comparison, and reuse of control experience, significantly enhancing agent reliability in long-horizon dynamic environments.

item.title: CircuitReason-1k: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Visual-to-Symbolic Reasoning inElectrical Circuits
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **CircuitReason-1k**, a benchmark of 1,000 authentic textbook problems designed to evaluate the complete long-horizon visual-to-symbolic reasoning pipeline in electrical circuit analysis—from grounding symbols and recovering topology to formulating equations and propagating physical quantities with correct units, signs, and conventions.
## Method & Evaluation Built via an evidence-first pipeline with strict question-figure-solution alignment, the benchmark uses a reasoning-oriented taxonomy to stratify problems by circuit type and dependency depth. We employ conservative typed scoring combined with identity-blinded multi-model semantic consensus, keeping all problems in the denominator.
## Key Results Across 3 commercial chatbots and 6 open-source multimodal LLMs, the best system achieves 84.8% accuracy. However, performance degrades consistently on long-horizon problems, with qualitative analysis revealing persistent failures in topology-to-target binding, physical conventions, and late-stage output propagation. This benchmark provides a focused testbed for measuring whether multimodal models can sustain physically valid symbolic reasoning from visual evidence. Code is publicly available.

item.title: FeedbackTrack: Visual-Cortex-Inspired Cross-Frame Feedback for Transformer Tracking
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **FeedbackTrack**, a visual-cortex-inspired framework that injects sparse, group-level, layer-aligned cross-frame feedback into pretrained Transformer trackers. Previous-frame intermediate states are detached, cached, and routed back via two lightweight pathways: Query Feedback (token-level modulation) and Gate Feedback (context-dependent feature gating), requiring only a one-frame cache.
## Key Results Across SPMTrack and ARTrackV2, FeedbackTrack consistently improves five backbone configurations on LaSOT and GOT-10k, achieving **83.4 AO** and **79.1 AUC** with SPMTrack-G while adding <1% parameters. Controlled comparisons show cross-frame feedback outperforms same-frame modulation by **1.8–3.2 AO**, confirming gains stem from recurrent historical information. Analysis further reveals non-uniform depth-dependent feedback strengths, demonstrating the effectiveness of recurrent feedback for transformer tracking.

item.title: Deep Learning based Detection of Fishing Vessels and Fishing Monitoring using Nightlight Images
item.description: This study presents a dual-branch YOLO11 model for detecting small-scale fishing vessels using SDGSAT-1 nighttime light imagery (10m panchromatic + 40m RGB), targeting the "dark vessel" challenge along India's western coast. The model achieved superior performance (precision 0.99, recall 0.93, F1 0.96, mAP@50 0.96) over single-branch baselines. Applied to 2022-23 data, it detected 31,525 vessels, of which 77.3% lacked AIS signals—identified as potential dark vessels. Spatio-temporal analysis revealed peak fishing during January-April within a 50-100km coastal corridor. This work demonstrates nightlight imagery's effectiveness for maritime surveillance and provides critical insights into fishing patterns and compliance gaps in Indian waters.
